newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-FLUMINENSE FANS SMASH CLUB HEADQUARTERS IN PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FLUMINENSE FANS SMASH CLUB HEADQUARTERS IN PROTEST.

text.p: Fluminense fans vandalised the restaurant and board room at their club's stadium after seeing their team fall two goals behind during a cup match on Wednesday.

Around 100 fans invaded the invaded the boardroom area of the stadium armed with sticks and stone and embarked on a wave of destruction, breaking nearly all the windows in two rooms at the Laranjeiras stadium.
They also invaded the directors' box in the stand and threatened club officials.
Two hundred riot police were called to restore order at the ground.
The club, who have had a dismal season in the Brazilian championship, last month took the precaution of putting iron railings over the stain-glass windows in the main stand.
The windows are frequently targeted by stone-throwing fans when the team does badly. However, directors did not appear to have counted on supporters getting inside.
The match was against Paraguayan side Guarany in the South American Conmebol Cup, the equivalent of Europe's Uefa Cup.
Guarany were already 3-1 ahead from the first match and increased the lead with goals by Edgar Baez and Artistides Rojas in a six minute spell in the first half.

Despite being jeered throughout the second half, Fluminense levelled the score on the night with goals by Paulo Roberto, through a penalty, and Hugo but went out 5-3 on aggregate to another chorus of jeers.
In the South American Supercup, played every year between past winners of the Libertadores, Argentine champions Velez Sarsfield and Cruzeiro of Brazil both ensured their places in the second round.
Velez beat Gremio, Libertadores champions last year, 1-0 with a last minute goal by substitute Christian Bassedas to go through 4-3 on aggregate.
Cruzeiro beat Uruguayans Nacional 3-1 to win 4-2 on aggregate.
